notes: Agent classes this proxy can reason about, with no fingerprints attached. A JA3 / JA4 / JA4H value is a measurement of one specific client build, and the published collections of those measurements carry their own licenses, so this file previously redistributed third-party licensed data inside an Apache-2.0 binary (WOR-2296). It now ships empty on purpose. An empty array means tls_fingerprint_matches() answers true, which is the conservative direction: detection is inert until an operator supplies values, and no client is accused of spoofing on the strength of a fingerprint we guessed at. Populate your own with proxy.extensions.tls_fingerprint.catalog_file, which replaces this file wholesale. request.tls.ja4 carries the value this proxy computed for the live handshake, so one known-good client through a CEL transform or an access-log field is one catalogue line. See docs/headless-detection.md.

entries.notes: Measure it yourself: serve a URL OpenAI's crawler already fetches and read request.tls.ja4 from the access log.
Anthropic publishes no JA4. Same approach as above.
Headless fingerprints track the bundled Chromium build, so a value is only true for the version you measured. Capture per Puppeteer release you care about rather than pinning one and trusting it.
